raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Part of #64418 (L3): write per-tensor expert scales and the Mamba v2 sharded conv1d/bias parameters with `Tensor.copy_` instead of index assignment, so a load plan or tracer sees the write. No change to loaded bytes. Depends on nothing; does not overlap #55091 (see Details).

## Claims

- The five index-assignment writes in these loaders now use `Tensor.copy_`, so tracing `load_weights` classifies them as direct writes instead of falling back (`write via __setitem__`).
- Loaded values are byte-identical to the previous index assignment, including `(1,)`-shaped per-tensor scales written into 0-D slots.
- On the L3 measurement (M0 trace, TP=1), fallback names drop: Qwen3-30B-A3B ModelOpt static per-tensor FP8 (synthetic header) 36,864 -> 0; Qwen3.5-4B 48 -> 24.

## Validation

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Expert scale loaders vs old index assignment, real `FusedMoEFactory` layer (Fp8 static per-tensor, 1 rank, GPU) | `pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_expert_scale_loading.py` | 10 passed (w13/w2 weight scale, w13/w2 input scale; 0-D and `(1,)` scales) |
| Mamba v2 sharded loader vs old index assignment (TP 2, and TP 4 with replicated groups) | `pytest -v -s tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_v2_sharded_loader.py` | 4 passed |
| Same tests on the unmodified nightly image (commit e0d00e4b8) | same commands | 14 passed (the new tests compare against the old behavior, so they also pass before the change) |
| Test catches a missing `reshape` | `_load_single_value` patched to `dst.copy_(loaded_weight)` with the new test | 2 failed: `RuntimeError: output with shape [] doesn't match the broadcast shape [1]` (`w13_input_scale`/`w2_input_scale` with `(1,)`) |
| Cold-start bytes, before vs after | `l3_verify.py` (sha256 of every parameter and buffer after `load_weights`) | identical for a tiny random MoE (ModelOpt static FP8, 57 tensors) and Qwen3.5-4B (671 tensors) |
| Direct reload | `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, begin -> `load_weights` -> finish | bytes equal to cold start, 0 tensors with a changed address, before and after the change |
| Fallback names, M0 trace | `m0_trace.py` | Qwen3-30B-A3B ModelOpt per-tensor FP8 (synthetic header): 36,864 -> 0 of 56,115 names. Qwen3.5-4B: 48 -> 24 (the 24 conv1d.weight now direct; 24 `linear_attn.norm.weight` remain fallback, separate cause) |
| Lint | `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (0.14.0), `typos` (1.51.1), `mypy --python-version 3.11` on the changed files | pass |

Not covered by unit tests (and by what): ModelOpt NVFP4 w13 `input_scale` two-slot branch (needs a Blackwell NVFP4 checkpoint to construct) and the ModelOpt per-tensor path; both are covered only by the end-to-end `l3_verify` byte comparison on the tiny ModelOpt-style MoE above, which does not exercise the NVFP4 branch. The change there is the same one-line `copy_` form. TP>1 is checked only for the Mamba loader (reference comparison); the MoE scale paths were run on TP=1.

## Details

Not a bug fix. `param[i] = x` already copied in place, so eager results are unchanged. The only difference is that it dispatches through `Tensor.__setitem__`, which a tracer that records `copy_` cannot see as a write; the loaded name then falls back to the slow path in a load plan.

`_load_single_value` also reshapes the source to the destination shape. Index assignment broadcast a `(1,)` checkpoint scale into a 0-D slot; `copy_` does not and would raise. The same function also loads the size-2 `weight_shape` (compressed-tensors), so `_to_scalar` is not reused. The "Assign directly" comment became "Copy directly".

`mamba_v2_sharded_weight_loader` previously assigned a slice; it now calls `copy_` on the same slice view. `kernels.yaml` adds `mamba_mixer2.py` to the Mamba kernels step's `source_file_dependencies` so the new test runs when the loader changes; the MoE test is picked up by the existing `kernels/moe` step.

#55091 changes only the shard computation inside `mamba_v2_sharded_weight_loader`; this PR only changes how the computed slice is written, so the two are independent and should rebase trivially.

Limitations: TP>1 not exercised end to end. The Qwen3-30B-A3B figure uses a synthetic header with real shapes, not a real checkpoint.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the patch, tests and measurements; I reviewed every changed line; the tests listed above were run on my test server (RTX 4090, vllm/vllm-openai nightly e0d00e4b8).

Thanks, the loader changes LGTM. Two asks:

1. Could you drop the two new test files and the `kernels.yaml` change? The tests compare against an inlined copy of the old loader, so they pass before and after (as noted in the description). They don't exercise the tracer, which is what L3 is about. That coverage comes from P2's per-family loopback test. The inlined Mamba shard math would also have to change in lockstep with #55091, and the `source_file_dependencies` entry triggers the GPU Mamba kernels step on every `mamba_mixer2.py` edit just to run a CPU-only test.
2. Could you also cover Inkling here? It's an RL family, and `load_expert_weight` in `vllm/models/inkling/{nvidia,amd}/moe.py` still writes the per-expert `_scale_2` / `_global_scale` scales, plus NVIDIA's per-channel `w2_weight_scale`, with `param.data[lids] = ...`. A plain `copy_` swap won't make these direct, because the index list, the `.float()` cast and the `expand` all make the name a fallback. They'd need a `narrow` + `copy_` per local expert in the checkpoint dtype. A checkpoint value shared by both w13 halves would become one `copy_` per half instead of an `expand`.

@@ -617,6 +617,7 @@ steps:
   - csrc/mamba/
   - tests/kernels/mamba
   - vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/checkpoint.py
+  - vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py
   - vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn
   - vllm/models/qwen3_5/
   - vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.mamba_mixer2 import (
+    mamba_v2_sharded_weight_loader,
+)
+
+
+def _index_assignment_loader(shard_spec, tp_size, tp_rank):
+    """The loader before it switched to ``copy_``."""
+
+    def loader(param, loaded_weight):
+        boundary, loaded_boundary = 0, 0
+        for full_dim, extra, duplicate_groups in shard_spec:
+            shard_size = full_dim // tp_size
+            loaded_skip = (0 if duplicate_groups else tp_rank) * shard_size
+            start = loaded_boundary + loaded_skip
+            take = min(shard_size, full_dim - extra - loaded_skip)
+            target = param.data[boundary : boundary + take]
+            param.data[boundary : boundary + take] = loaded_weight[
+                start : start + take
+            ].view_as(target)
+            boundary += shard_size
+            loaded_boundary += full_dim - extra
+
+    return loader
+
+
+# (full_dim, extra, duplicate_groups) per segment, e.g. x / B / C of conv1d.
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "shard_spec,tp_size",
+    [
+        ([(16, 0, False), (8, 0, False), (8, 0, False)], 2),
+        # n_groups == 1 replicated across ranks
+        ([(16, 0, False), (8, 4, True), (8, 4, True)], 4),
+    ],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("trailing", [(), (3,)])  # bias / conv1d weight
+def test_loader_matches_index_assignment(shard_spec, tp_size, trailing):
+    full = sum(dim - extra for dim, extra, _ in shard_spec)
+    local = sum(dim // tp_size for dim, _, _ in shard_spec)
+    loaded = torch.randn(full, *trailing)
+    for tp_rank in range(tp_size):
+        expected = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.full((local, *trailing), -7.0))
+        got = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.full((local, *trailing), -7.0))
+        _index_assignment_loader(shard_spec, tp_size, tp_rank)(expected, loaded)
+        mamba_v2_sharded_weight_loader(shard_spec, tp_size, tp_rank)(got, loaded)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)

@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Per-tensor expert scale loading writes the same bytes as index assignment."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.layer import FusedMoEFactory
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.fp8 import Fp8Config
+
+EXPERT_ID = 2
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def fp8_static_experts(dist_init, default_vllm_config, workspace_init):
+    layer = FusedMoEFactory(
+        num_experts=4,
+        top_k=2,
+        hidden_size=256,
+        intermediate_size=512,
+        params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        quant_config=Fp8Config(
+            is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized=True, activation_scheme="static"
+        ),
+        prefix="model.layers.0.mlp.experts",
+    )
+    return layer.routed_experts
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scale_shape", [(), (1,)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "param_name,shard_id",
+    [
+        ("w13_weight_scale", "w1"),
+        ("w13_weight_scale", "w3"),
+        ("w2_weight_scale", "w2"),
+        ("w13_input_scale", "w1"),
+        ("w2_input_scale", "w2"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_per_tensor_scale_matches_index_assignment(
+    fp8_static_experts, param_name, shard_id, scale_shape
+):
+    param = getattr(fp8_static_experts, param_name)
+    scale = torch.full(scale_shape, 0.25)
+
+    # What the loaders did before: ``param[expert][shard] = scale``.
+    expected = param.data.clone()
+    if param_name == "w13_weight_scale":
+        expected[EXPERT_ID][0 if shard_id == "w1" else 1] = scale
+    else:
+        expected[EXPERT_ID] = scale
+
+    assert param.weight_loader(
+        param, scale, param_name, shard_id, EXPERT_ID, return_success=True
+    )
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(param.data, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)

@@ -370,10 +370,10 @@ def _load_per_tensor_weight_scale(
             # We have to keep the weight scales of w1 and w3 because
             # we need to re-quantize w1/w3 weights after weight loading.
             idx = 0 if shard_id == "w1" else 1
-            param_data[expert_id][idx] = self._to_scalar(loaded_weight)
+            param_data[expert_id][idx].copy_(self._to_scalar(loaded_weight))
         # If we are in the row parallel case (down_proj)
         elif shard_id == "w2":
-            param_data[expert_id] = self._to_scalar(loaded_weight)
+            param_data[expert_id].copy_(self._to_scalar(loaded_weight))
 
     def _load_combined_w13_weight_scale(
         self,
@@ -657,9 +657,10 @@ def _load_single_value(
         param_data = param.data
 
         # Used for both scalar input_scale and the size-2 `weight_shape`
-        # param (compressed-tensors). Assign directly so both shapes load;
+        # param (compressed-tensors). Copy directly so both shapes load;
         # _to_scalar's reshape(()) would reject the size-2 weight_shape.
-        param_data[expert_id] = loaded_weight
+        dst = param_data[expert_id]
+        dst.copy_(loaded_weight.reshape(dst.shape))
 
     @overload
     def weight_loader(
@@ -838,8 +839,8 @@ def weight_loader(
             ):
                 scale_expert_id = global_expert_id if use_global_sf else expert_id
                 scale_shard_id = 0 if shard_id == "w1" else 1
-                param.data[scale_expert_id][scale_shard_id] = self._to_scalar(
-                    loaded_weight
+                param.data[scale_expert_id][scale_shard_id].copy_(
+                    self._to_scalar(loaded_weight)
                 )
                 return True if return_success else None

@@ -245,13 +245,13 @@ def loader(param: torch.Tensor, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor) -> None:
             #   seem to handle slices well.
             # https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2410
             target_slice = param.data[boundary : (boundary + take), ...]
-            param.data[
-                boundary : (boundary + take), ...  # type: ignore[misc]
-            ] = loaded_weight[
-                loaded_start_idx : (
-                    loaded_start_idx + take
-                )  # type: ignore[misc]
-            ].view_as(target_slice)
+            target_slice.copy_(
+                loaded_weight[
+                    loaded_start_idx : (
+                        loaded_start_idx + take
+                    )  # type: ignore[misc]
+                ].view_as(target_slice)
+            )
 
             # move indexing boundaries
             boundary += shard_size
